as_of.score_formula: 100 * sum(w_i * d_i for observed i) / sum(w_i for observed i) / 2, with d_i in {-2,-1,+1,+2}
as_of.current_stance_formula: decay-weighted average of agreed event scores in the 90-day window; weight = 0.5 ** (days / 30)
as_of.disagreement_rule: Agree only if Pass A and Pass B match on the sign of the event score and on every observed dimension, and coverage differs by less than 20 percentage points. Otherwise do not average; mark 'disagreement – analyst review'. A dimension observed in only one pass stays not_observed until analyst confirmation.
vorbehalte: Weights (40/20/20/10/10), camp thresholds (±20), alert thresholds (15 / 25 points) and the 30-day half-life are proposed model parameters and are not validated (nicht validiert / not validated).

Every scored quote used on the public site is verbatim from an official Board or Reserve Bank page or PDF stored in this package. Licensed-press wording (including the Phase 1 Schmid 10.11 pointer) is not in site_data.

Interviews without an official transcript are unconfirmed and are not scored. That includes the 14.10 Daly Hoover appearance (official coverage page, no transcript), the 8.10 Musalem moderated Q&A (official event page is a short third-person summary, not a transcript), and an 18.11 Waller appearance for which no Board transcript was found.

Speeches without monetary-policy path or stance content are excluded from the public events table (including Musalem 6.10 community-banking remarks, 14.10 Open Vault blog, 6.11 decentralised-by-design; supervisory, payments and ceremonial Board and Reserve Bank remarks).

The official 29.09 Musalem 'How and Why' prepared-remarks body is incomplete in this package (Firecrawl result truncated after curl to stlouisfed.org timed out). Official key takeaways were retrieved in full and are the public quote. Error E20261120-dc2e is left open for this residual gap.

Phase 1 labelled Logan's 30.10 Davidson remarks as partial; the official text contains the same counted path as 10.11 and is scored in Phase 2. Primary-source dates are used throughout. Pre-screen date deviations remain: Williams path language is official on 29.09, not 13.10; the 10.11 Schmid pre-screen wording was not found on the official 15.11 transcript; the 14.10 Daly pre-screen wording was not verified on a primary transcript.

Missing dimensions are coded 'not observed', never 0. The allowed dimension codes are {-2,-1,+1,+2} or not_observed. An explicitly balanced or two-sided statement (Jefferson 19.11; parts of Barkin 9.11) cannot be coded 0 and is recorded as not observed, with the effect that coverage is not credited.

Event scores are computed from observed dimensions only, with weights renormalised over those dimensions and then scaled by 1/2 to the -100..+100 range. A single observed dimension therefore renormalises to ±50 or ±100. Coverage and confidence are published with the score; a high score with low coverage is not a high-confidence reading.

Where Pass A and Pass B disagree on any observed dimension, on sign, or on coverage by 20 percentage points or more, the event has no published final score (no averaging). Current stance uses agreed events only. Pass-specific stances are shown and are not averaged. Camp changes and counter-lean alerts require analyst sign-off; none are issued, because structural lean is 'insufficient history' in this 90-day sample.

Structural lean is not computed: the spec requires 12–18 months of evidence across different data regimes, which were not fetched in Phase 2. Camps printed on current stance are not structural classifications.

2026 voter status is taken from the official FOMC membership page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomc.htm, last update 18 November 2026). Among the ten names, voters are Logan, Waller, Hammack, Bowman, Williams and Jefferson. Musalem and Schmid are not 2026 voters. Daly and Barkin are listed as 2026 alternate members.

Relative shift is a diagnostic (own change minus the median change of peers with a defined agreed change), not a causal estimate. Several people have no agreed pre-event baseline, so no change and no relative shift.
Panel A bubble size is the number of official, policy-relevant, verbatim-text evidence items in the 90-day window, not a market-influence weight.
No FRED or other API key, and no licensed dataset, is in this package. Firecrawl was used only for targeted official St. Louis Fed pages and PDFs after curl timed out.

A successful run of the scoring script proves that the arithmetic identities were executed, not that the dimension codes are financially or institutionally 'correct'. Dimension codes are analyst-style AI judgments from the stored official text, awaiting the later validation workstream in the build plan.

scores.title: Remarks to Davidson College students
scores.a_rationale: Prepared student remarks contain the same explicit path as her later Houston speech: at least two more 25bp increases, and the funds-rate range at least 50bp below modest restriction. Skipping the October meeting does not change the destination; she does not pin the next increment to a named meeting. No explicit balance-of-risks ranking. A short data-dependence clause is not treated as a scored reaction-function design.
scores.b_rationale: The official Davidson remarks state a counted path (at least two more 25bp increases) and a restrictiveness diagnosis (funds-rate range at least 50bp below modest restriction). The October skip is said not to change the destination; no named next-meeting date is given, so timing is only moderately hawkish. No explicit risk ranking is offered.

scores.title: Economic and monetary policy outlook
scores.a_rationale: Explicit path: at least two more 25bp increases; destination unchanged by the October skip. Policy is assessed as accommodative and as adding to inflationary pressures; the funds-rate range is at least 50bp below modest restriction. Timing of each increment is downplayed relative to the destination. Reaction function not separately observed beyond the path itself.
scores.b_rationale: Same counted path and restrictiveness diagnosis as on 30 October, plus an explicit statement that accommodative policy is adding to inflationary pressures. Destination is unchanged by the skip. No separate reaction-function design is laid out.

scores.title: The Economic Outlook and Some Comments on My Policy Communication
scores.a_rationale: Near-term path is stated only as conditionals: inclined to hold if August inflation progress continues, and a hike may be appropriate if that improvement proves fleeting. Under the spec, conditionals are not the baseline, so preferred path and timing are not observed. Upside inflation risks are stated; activity and the labor market 'are not a large factor'. Policy is 'currently only slightly restricting aggregate demand'. He explains that reaction function explicitly.
scores.b_rationale: Although both hold and hike are conditional on August inflation, he also says policy is only slightly restricting demand and that it may not take much inflation acceleration to nudge him into tighter policy, with labor and activity 'not a large factor'. That is treated as a mild tightening bias on the preferred path, not as an unobserved dimension. Timing is still not observed (the September meeting is the decision date, not an urgency claim). Upside inflation risks and the slightly-restrictive assessment are observed, as is the stated reaction function.

scores.title: The Signaling Value of the Summary of Economic Projections
scores.a_rationale: The speech is mainly about how to communicate a path. The 'three 25bp hikes / 75bp over six months' figures are introduced with 'let's assume' as an illustration, not as his baseline recommendation, so they are not scored as a preferred path. He does explain a data-dependent way of signaling a likely terminal increment. Forward path, timing, current risk balance and current restrictiveness are not observed as his own baseline.
scores.b_rationale: The 75bp / three-hike figures are presented as an assumed illustration of communication methods ('let's assume'), not as Waller's own baseline path, and are not scored as a path. A data-dependent way of signaling a likely total increment is a reaction-function/communication observation only.

scores.title: The Economic Outlook and Some Thoughts on Labor Market Dynamism
scores.a_rationale: Baseline is a 25bp increase at the December meeting even if October inflation improves. A 50bp December hike is explicitly conditional on October CPI coming in like the last two prints (core CPI around 0.3 percent or higher) and is therefore not the baseline path. Tightening is needed 'sooner rather than later'. Inflation is 'the focus of my attention'. Further tightening is needed, which is scored as policy not yet tight enough. The 50bp threshold is a stated reaction-function branch.
scores.b_rationale: His plan if things proceed as expected is +25bp in December, even if inflation improves. The 50bp option is a stated branch if October core CPI is around 0.3 percent or higher, and is not the baseline path. 'Sooner rather than later' and the December date are a strong timing signal. Inflation is the focus of attention; further tightening is needed.

scores.title: Trimming the Sails: Communicating My Reaction Function
scores.a_rationale: She says a restrictive stance will be needed, in a timely fashion, given risks to the inflation side of the mandate. That is a destination, not a counted increment. She states that explaining her reaction function is not a policy prediction. Elevated inflation relative to her forecast could require still higher policy rates. Current policy is implied not yet restrictive enough.
scores.b_rationale: A restrictive stance is needed, in a timely fashion, with risks on the inflation side. No hike count. Conditionality of the reaction function is explained, including a higher-rate branch if inflation stays elevated relative to her forecast.

scores.title: Reserve Currencies and Stablecoins
scores.a_rationale: Pre-screen path language is present: policy needs to move to a restrictive stance in a timely manner, preferably via more frequent smaller adjustments. No explicit current risk ranking or reaction-function design beyond that pace preference, which is not scored as a separate reaction-function observation.
scores.b_rationale: Move to a restrictive stance in a timely manner, preferably with more frequent smaller adjustments. No risk-balance or reaction-function paragraph is used beyond that destination and pace preference.

scores.title: How and Why
scores.a_rationale: Official key takeaways (retrieved in full) and the retrieved body describe a communications framework, not a current funds-rate path. He explicitly sets aside 'forward guidance of a specific policy path'. An 18-month horizon appears as a framework element, not as current tightening urgency. Preferred path, timing, risks and restrictiveness are not observed. The reaction-function/framework discussion is observed. The stored prepared-remarks body is incomplete (Firecrawl result truncated); scores use only the retrieved official takeaways and retrieved body and are flagged as such.
scores.b_rationale: The official key takeaways reject promising a specific policy path and present a how-and-why framework instead. Only the reaction-function/framework dimension is observed. The stored prepared-remarks body is incomplete; this pass uses the complete official takeaways and the retrieved body only.

scores.title: Remarks on the U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
scores.a_rationale: He judges that additional firming will be necessary, and soon, without giving a hike count, so the path code is +1 not +2. Inflation risks are 'skewed toward persistent above-target inflation'. Policy and financial conditions 'remain accommodative'. The more likely 18-month scenario requires further firming; a second scenario without firming is described as less likely. He prefers moving sooner in smaller steps.
scores.b_rationale: Additional firming is necessary, and soon, without a counted increment (path +1). 'Skewed toward persistent above-target inflation' is an inflation-side risk lean, scored +1 rather than +2 because it is a skew, not a statement that employment risk is absent. Policy remains accommodative. The two-scenario structure, with firming as the more likely case, is a reaction-function observation.

scores.title: Remarks on the U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
scores.a_rationale: Later and more quantitative: several interest-rate increases before spring 2027, and soon. Risks remain skewed toward persistent above-target inflation. Current policy is 'not yet restraining inflation'; the real policy rate is at the lower end of 1–1.5% versus a needed 2–2.5%. The two-scenario reaction-function structure is restated, with the firming scenario treated as the more likely baseline.
scores.b_rationale: Several interest-rate increases before spring 2027, and soon, is a counted tighter path. Current policy is not yet restraining inflation; the real-rate gap (about 1–1.5% versus 2–2.5%) supports a strong accommodative/too-easy reading. Risks are again 'skewed' toward persistent above-target inflation, scored +1 (a skew, not a one-sided extreme). The same two-scenario reaction function is restated.

scores.title: The Economic Outlook, Monetary Policy and Payments
scores.a_rationale: Official text says inflation is running too hot and 'we have work to do', and rejects the idea that inflation is beyond the Fed's power to control. Under the spec, 'inflation is too high / work to do' is not scored as a preferred path. No increment, meeting date, or restrictiveness assessment appears in the official remarks. The labor market is described as close to full employment while inflation is the problem, which is a mild inflation-side risk observation. The phrase used in the 10.11 pre-screen is not in this official text and is not used here.
scores.b_rationale: The official remarks document that inflation is too high and that the Fed has work to do, but the spec says inflation-above-target language alone is not a strong hawk signal and is not a preferred path. There is no explicit balance-of-risks ranking, no restrictiveness assessment, no timing, and no reaction-function design. All five dimensions are not observed, so there is no numeric event score. The 10.11 pre-screen phrasing is absent from this official text and is not used.

scores.title: The U.S. Economy and Considerations for Monetary Policy
scores.a_rationale: She supported the October hold and said further rate changes should wait until the September increase was better understood. She now sees inflation pressures persisting and labor firming, and is 'more attentive to the inflation side', with 'still work to do' to bring inflation closer to 2 percent. That is not an explicit December increment; the spec treats inflation-above-target language without a path request as not a strong path signal. She also says the benefit of additional tightening has to be weighed against costs, and that policy is not on a preset course.
scores.b_rationale: No explicit path request: she supported the October hold, says additional tightening must be weighed against costs, and says policy is not on a preset course. 'Work to do' on inflation is not scored as a path. She is more attentive to the inflation side, which is a risk-balance observation. Data-dependence / not a preset course is a reaction-function observation.

scores.title: Unwavering Dedication
scores.a_rationale: His forecast-consistent baseline is that one further upward adjustment may be appropriate late this year. That is treated as a baseline path, not a tail scenario, though it remains conditional on the forecast. After the September hike he sees 'no need for urgency' and time to gather more information, so timing is scored as non-urgent. Employment risk has receded and the risk to price stability has increased. Current restrictiveness is not assessed in so many words.
scores.b_rationale: The one-further-adjustment sentence is explicitly conditional on the economy evolving in line with his forecast, and he immediately adds that 'that is just my forecast'. Under the spec, conditionals are not the baseline, so preferred path is not observed. 'No need for urgency' is a clear timing observation. The risk shift (employment risk receded, price-stability risk increased) is observed. Restrictiveness is not assessed.

scores.title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
scores.a_rationale: He supported the already-taken September 25bp increase. Future adjustments are data-, outlook- and risk-dependent, with no December or 6–12 month increment. Activity and employment risks are roughly balanced; inflation risks are to the upside.
scores.b_rationale: Support for the already-taken September hike is not a forward path. Future adjustments are data-dependent. Upside inflation risks are stated alongside roughly balanced activity and employment risks.

scores.title: New Technology, Old Questions: Productivity Puzzles and the Macroeconomy
scores.a_rationale: A productivity speech whose policy close says the inflation trajectory is the more important signal for the stance, and that further adjustments depend on data, the outlook and risks. No preferred path, timing, current risk ranking, or current restrictiveness assessment is given. The r* discussion is general and is not scored as a current restrictiveness call.
scores.b_rationale: Only a reaction-function close is observed: the inflation trajectory is the more important signal, and further adjustments depend on data, the outlook and risks. No path, timing, current risk ranking or restrictiveness call.

scores.title: Monetary Policy amid Frequent and Complex Shocks
scores.a_rationale: Short prepared remarks on how to respond to supply and demand shocks. The 'stronger reaction to inflation' language is explicitly conditional on unanchored inflation expectations, and is paired with the opposite branch (prioritize employment downside if price pressures are contained). There is no baseline path, timing, current risk ranking, or restrictiveness call. Because the reaction function is two-sided and the scale has no 0, it is recorded as not observed rather than as a hawkish pivot. No numeric event score is computed (coverage 0).
scores.b_rationale: A two-sided conditional reaction function with no baseline path. 'Stronger reaction to inflation' is not scored as a hawkish pivot. Because the coding scale has no 0, an explicitly two-sided function is recorded as not observed. Coverage is zero; no numeric event score.

scores.title: Why Hike?
scores.a_rationale: He explains the already-taken September hike: inflation risks outweigh maximum-employment risks. On the future path he asks 'Will additional hikes be required, and how many? We'll see.' That is not a preferred forward path. Timing language refers to why the last hike happened, not to a future increment.
scores.b_rationale: Inflation risks outweigh employment risks, which is why they raised rates. That is an observed inflation-side lean, scored +1 rather than +2 because he still treats employment as an active side of the mandate and leaves the future path open ('We'll see'). No forward path or future timing is stated.

scores.title: The Rooms Driving the Economy
scores.a_rationale: He says the appropriate direction is 'relatively straightforward' given healthy demand and stubborn inflation, but immediately qualifies that demand risks remain easy to envision and that 'it is wise to move policy with care.' There is no meeting-dated path, so preferred path is not observed. 'With care' is scored as non-urgent timing. The risk discussion is two-sided and is not coded (the scale has no 0).
scores.b_rationale: The 'appropriate direction' is implied to be tighter, but he gives no increment and immediately stresses demand risks and moving 'with care'. That combination is the pre-screen 'indeterminate' case: no preferred path, and 'with care' is not coded as a standalone timing stance because it qualifies an unstated path rather than dating an action. The risk discussion is two-sided, and the scale has no 0, so risks are not observed. No numeric event score.

vorbehalte: Weights (40/20/20/10/10), camp thresholds (±20), alert thresholds (15 / 25 points) and the 30-day half-life are proposed model parameters and are not validated (nicht validiert / not validated).

Every scored quote used on the public site is verbatim from an official Board or Reserve Bank page or PDF stored in this package. Licensed-press wording (including the Phase 1 Schmid 10.11 pointer) is not in site_data.

Interviews without an official transcript are unconfirmed and are not scored. That includes the 14.10 Daly Hoover appearance (official coverage page, no transcript), the 8.10 Musalem moderated Q&A (official event page is a short third-person summary, not a transcript), and an 18.11 Waller appearance for which no Board transcript was found.

Speeches without monetary-policy path or stance content are excluded from the public events table (including Musalem 6.10 community-banking remarks, 14.10 Open Vault blog, 6.11 decentralised-by-design; supervisory, payments and ceremonial Board and Reserve Bank remarks).

The official 29.09 Musalem 'How and Why' prepared-remarks body is incomplete in this package (Firecrawl result truncated after curl to stlouisfed.org timed out). Official key takeaways were retrieved in full and are the public quote. Error E20261120-dc2e is left open for this residual gap.

Phase 1 labelled Logan's 30.10 Davidson remarks as partial; the official text contains the same counted path as 10.11 and is scored in Phase 2. Primary-source dates are used throughout. Pre-screen date deviations remain: Williams path language is official on 29.09, not 13.10; the 10.11 Schmid pre-screen wording was not found on the official 15.11 transcript; the 14.10 Daly pre-screen wording was not verified on a primary transcript.

Missing dimensions are coded 'not observed', never 0. The allowed dimension codes are {-2,-1,+1,+2} or not_observed. An explicitly balanced or two-sided statement (Jefferson 19.11; parts of Barkin 9.11) cannot be coded 0 and is recorded as not observed, with the effect that coverage is not credited.

Event scores are computed from observed dimensions only, with weights renormalised over those dimensions and then scaled by 1/2 to the -100..+100 range. A single observed dimension therefore renormalises to ±50 or ±100. Coverage and confidence are published with the score; a high score with low coverage is not a high-confidence reading.

Where Pass A and Pass B disagree on any observed dimension, on sign, or on coverage by 20 percentage points or more, the event has no published final score (no averaging). Current stance uses agreed events only. Pass-specific stances are shown and are not averaged. Camp changes and counter-lean alerts require analyst sign-off; none are issued, because structural lean is 'insufficient history' in this 90-day sample.

Structural lean is not computed: the spec requires 12–18 months of evidence across different data regimes, which were not fetched in Phase 2. Camps printed on current stance are not structural classifications.

2026 voter status is taken from the official FOMC membership page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomc.htm, last update 18 November 2026). Among the ten names, voters are Logan, Waller, Hammack, Bowman, Williams and Jefferson. Musalem and Schmid are not 2026 voters. Daly and Barkin are listed as 2026 alternate members.

Relative shift is a diagnostic (own change minus the median change of peers with a defined agreed change), not a causal estimate. Several people have no agreed pre-event baseline, so no change and no relative shift.
Panel A bubble size is the number of official, policy-relevant, verbatim-text evidence items in the 90-day window, not a market-influence weight.
No FRED or other API key, and no licensed dataset, is in this package. Firecrawl was used only for targeted official St. Louis Fed pages and PDFs after curl timed out.

A successful run of the scoring script proves that the arithmetic identities were executed, not that the dimension codes are financially or institutionally 'correct'. Dimension codes are analyst-style AI judgments from the stored official text, awaiting the later validation workstream in the build plan.
